subject: General Knowledge
topic: Nobel laureates — Indian connection — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Amartya Sen became the first Asian to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences. In which year was this honour awarded to him?

options.option_text: 1995, for contributions to social choice theory
1998, for contributions to welfare economics
2001, for his work on development economics
2005, for the capabilities approach to poverty

questions.explanation: Amartya Sen received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory. The year 2001 is a common distractor because Joseph Stiglitz (with Akerlof and Spence) won that year and also worked on development themes, but Sen's prize was three years earlier.

questions.stem: Rabindranath Tagore's 'Gitanjali', the work that earned him the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature, was originally composed in which language?

options.option_text: Sanskrit, the classical language of ancient Indian texts
Hindi, India's most widely spoken modern language
Bengali, the regional language of Bengal and Bangladesh
Marathi, the language of Maharashtra in western India

questions.explanation: Tagore originally wrote 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings) in Bengali; he himself translated a selection into English prose-poems, and this English version caught the attention of W. B. Yeats, who wrote its introduction. Sanskrit is wrong because Tagore was a modern Bengali poet, not a Sanskrit scholar.

questions.stem: Kailash Satyarthi, who shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai, founded which organisation in 1980 to combat child labour in India?

options.option_text: CRY (Child Rights and You), a Mumbai-based NGO
Bal Vikas Ashram, which rehabilitates rescued child labourers
Bachpan Bachao Andolan, the Save the Childhood movement
Child Labour Project, administered under ILO South Asia office

questions.explanation: Satyarthi founded Bachpan Bachao Andolan (BBA) in 1980; the movement has rescued over 90,000 children from bonded labour and trafficking. CRY (Child Rights and You) is a well-known child-rights NGO but was founded separately and was not Satyarthi's organisation.

questions.stem: Ronald Ross, who won the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for proving that malaria is transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, conducted his landmark dissection experiments in which Indian city?

options.option_text: Calcutta, where the Indian Medical Service headquarters was located
Secunderabad, at the military cantonment hospital in Hyderabad State
Bombay, at the Grant Medical College and its attached hospital
Madras, at the Government General Hospital pathology department

questions.explanation: Ross performed his decisive experiment on 20 August 1897 in Secunderabad (present-day Hyderabad, Telangana), dissecting Anopheles mosquitoes fed on malaria patients and finding the parasite in their stomach walls. Calcutta is a common distractor because Ross also worked there, but the key experiment was done in Secunderabad.

questions.stem: Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo, who shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economics with Michael Kremer, are credited with pioneering which research methodology in the study of global poverty?

options.option_text: Computable general equilibrium modelling of national economies
Randomised controlled trials applied to development economics
Dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) analysis method
Input-output analysis applied to agricultural supply chain gaps

questions.explanation: Banerjee, Duflo, and Kremer pioneered the use of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) — the gold standard of clinical research — to rigorously test anti-poverty interventions in the field. CGE and DSGE models are macroeconomic tools associated with other Nobel laureates such as Prescott and Kydland, not with poverty-alleviation field experiments.

questions.stem: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Thomas Steitz and Ada Yonath for using X-ray crystallography to determine the atomic-level structure of which cellular machine?

options.option_text: DNA polymerase III, the enzyme replicating chromosomal DNA
The ribosome, which decodes messenger RNA into proteins
RNA polymerase II, which transcribes protein-coding genes
The proteasome, degrading ubiquitin-tagged cellular proteins

questions.explanation: Ramakrishnan, Steitz, and Yonath solved the three-dimensional structure of the ribosome at atomic resolution, revealing exactly how it reads mRNA codons and assembles amino acid chains — enabling rational design of antibiotics. RNA polymerase is a common distractor because it also acts on RNA, but it is a transcription enzyme, not a translation machine.

questions.stem: A NASA X-ray space observatory launched in 1999 was named after which Indian-born Nobel laureate who computed the upper mass limit for white dwarf stars?

options.option_text: C.V. Raman, who discovered inelastic light scattering in 1928
Har Gobind Khorana, who cracked the triplet genetic code in 1968
Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, astrophysicist and 1983 Nobel laureate
Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, who mapped ribosomal structure in 2009

questions.explanation: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory (launched July 1999) is named after Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, who won the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for showing that a white dwarf exceeding ~1.4 solar masses (the Chandrasekhar Limit) cannot be supported by electron degeneracy pressure and will collapse further into a neutron star or black hole. C.V. Raman is the most tempting distractor as he was also a famous Indian physicist Nobel laureate, but no major NASA telescope is named after him.
